To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the S-bilayers of the HFBI protein form spontaneously from the solution, that the S-bilirayers are stable in the absence of the protein solution, and that their formation is accompanied by the energy gain that exceeds the energy of the formation of the liquid film by an order of magnitude.

the HFBII protein forms a bilayer with a hydrophobic core and hydrophilic surface, and this bilayer is formed by a strong hydrophobic interaction between the "hydrophobic" parts of the protein molecules.
the hydrophobin protein forms a S-bilayer at the air/wa-ter interface, which is stabilized by hydrophobic interactions between the hydrophilic domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the adhesion of the hydrophobins, which is a unique example of the formation of a self-assembled protein bilayer.
the mechanism of hydrophobic interaction between hydrophilic molecules.
the mechanism of adhesion of HFBII molecules and their self-assembly into S-bilayers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HFBII S-bilayer is formed due to hydrophobic interaction of hydrophilic domains of the protein molecules, which is accompanied by an energy gain of 0.6 kT per protein molecule.
the S-bilayers from HFBII are formed by a combination of hydrophobic attraction and hydrophobic interaction, and the latter is dominant at least in the pH range from 4.0 to 6.0.
the adhesion energy of HFBII bilayer is due to a short-range interaction between the hydrophilic domains of the HFB molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S-bilayer formation is the result of the competition between the attractive hydrophobic and repulsive electrostatic interactions between the protein molecules.
the S-bilayer of HFBII is formed due to the hydrophobic attraction of the hydrophobic parts of the protein, while the hydrophilic parts are attracted to the water.
hydrophobicity is an important factor in the formation of the S-bilayer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S-bilayer is a stable and robust structure that can be formed by the HFBII proteins in the absence of other proteins, lipids, or other additives.
the formation of the HFB-II bilayer film is a spontaneous process that occurs with a considerable energy gain.
the HFBII protein molecules can form stable S-bilayers with a thickness of about 6 nm.
